newsitem.title: UK: European bourses dip as Dow falls again.
newsitem.headline: European bourses dip as Dow falls again.

text.p: European bourses, which had drifted flat or mixed in thin trade all day, closed generally lower on Monday as Wall Street slid again in morning New York trade after its near 60-point setback on Friday.
The early weakness in the U.S. did nothing to help sentiment in Europe, where investors had been pondering whether they are seeing the beginning of the end of the bull market.

On the currency front the dollar ended steady in quiet trading just below the sessions highs, a contrast to the frantic currency trading of last week which took the U.S. currency to multi-year peaks against the mark and the yen.

In London, Europe's busiest stock exchange, shares which had been flat most of the morning dropped to close in negative territory after Wall Street moved lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 32 points or nearly half a percent as London closed.
Investors here were wary, unsure whether New York could be on the verge of a more substantial downside correction.
"There hasn't been a lot of selling but marketmakers are on their guard," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
"People are talking about Wall Street coming off several hundred points and don't want to be around if that happens."
The blue chip FTSE 100 has some support at around the 4,200 level and a move below that area could attract some near-term buying, dealers said. It closed at 4,212.0.
J Sainsbury, which plunged 13 percent after a profits warning on Friday, once again led supermarket shares lower on worries about a possible full-scale price war.

Earlier, British equities and gilts had showed little reaction to the latest British gross domestic product figures showing the economy grew 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter for annual growth of 2.6 percent in 1996.

The statistics, which were in line with analysts' expectations, should reinforce growing market confidence that base rates will not rise ahead of the general election, which must take place by May 22, analysts said.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended the bourse session slightly lower before the Dow opened. Trading volumes had been low with some dealers saying they saw the threat of further declines. But the firm dollar, which is good for German exports, was providing some support and enabled the IBIS DAX index of electronic trading to close up, though off its highs of the day.

In Paris, French stocks also lost most of their gains after New York's open but still managed to close up a few points. One boost for Paris stocks had come from Rhone-Poulenc, which jumped after its unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer reported good 1996 results.

The dollar was just above 1.64 marks in late European trade -- it had touched 1.6429 earlier in the day -- but dealers said trade was thin and rangebound conditions were likely to continue. The market seemed reluctant to retest the multi-year highs reached last week and was catching its breath before a possible attempt to go higher, dealers said.
"It should stay rangebound for the next couple of days," said a dealer at a Swiss bank in London. "It's corrective, but not a reversal."

U.S. employment cost data, due on Tuesday, was the focus for now, analysts said, as the results could provide indications on the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) decision on interest rates at its next meeting on February 4 and 5.

"The Fed likes to watch the quarterly employment cost index closely. The monthly earnings data are more narrowly based, but provide good clues," said Robin Aspinall, strategist at National Australia Bank.
The fourth-quarter employment cost index is forecast to rise by 1.2 percent after a 0.6 percent increase the previous quarter, according to a Reuters poll of economists.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was at 119.40 yen and 1.6412 marks compared with late Europe's Friday level of 118.93 yen and 1.6265 marks.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 6.8 points lower at 4,212.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 4.83 at 2,435.17.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 3.71 at 2,994.53.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended in London at $354.60 compared with its Friday London close of $353.35 an ounce.
